AFAM 200.description: A study of the United States founding documents that emphasizes how the experiences of African American citizens throughout history and culture shape the country’s values, norms, and ideals.
AFAM 200.subject: AFAM
AFAM 200.title: Freedom Papers: Narratives of Race and Nation

AFAM 201.description: Introduction to the key debates, figures, and concepts that are fundamental to the interdisciplinary study of the historical, political, and social development of black life in America.
AFAM 201.subject: AFAM
AFAM 201.title: Introduction to African American Studies: Social and Historical Foundations

AFAM 202.description: Introduction to the analysis and discussion of creative works and traditions by and about African Americans through folklore, music, art, dance, and literature.
AFAM 202.subject: AFAM
AFAM 202.title: Introduction to African-American Studies

AFAM 207.description: The variety of religious traditions of African Americans, with emphasis on the contexts in which they developed.
AFAM 207.subject: AFAM
AFAM 207.title: Introduction to African American Religions

AFAM 218.description: An examination of African American and Jewish American inter-ethnic, historical and contemporary connections and disconnections. Implications for educational, social, and social settings are considered.
AFAM 218.subject: AFAM
AFAM 218.title: Convergence and Divergence in African American and Jewish Relations: Historical and Contemporary

AFAM 303.description: An examination of African-American cultures in the New World.
AFAM 303.subject: AFAM
AFAM 303.title: African-American Cultures

AFAM 308.description: An interdisciplinary survey of the contributions of African-American women to feminist theory.
AFAM 308.subject: AFAM
AFAM 308.title: African-American Feminist Theory

AFAM 330.description: Psychological theory and research as it applies to African Americans. Explores Africentric and other perspectives and roles of culture, racism, and historical phenomena.
AFAM 330.subject: AFAM
AFAM 330.title: Psychology and the African-American Experience

AFAM 331.description: The social, cultural, economic, and political life of black people in the United States to 1865.
AFAM 331.subject: AFAM
AFAM 331.title: Black Experience in the United States to 1865

AFAM 332.description: The social, cultural, economic, and political life of black people in the United States since 1865.
AFAM 332.subject: AFAM
AFAM 332.title: Black Experience in the United States since 1865

AFAM 335.description: Examination of the origins of Jim Crow and the multi-faceted struggle against it, and other forms of racial inequality, in the American South and the rest of the US since the early 20th century.
AFAM 335.subject: AFAM
AFAM 335.title: The American Civil Rights Movement

AFAM 343.description: Explore development/theologies of African/African Diaspora religions; examine misunderstandings; arrive at a more sophisticated and nuanced vision of these religions and the people who hold them.
AFAM 343.subject: AFAM
AFAM 343.title: Religions of the African Diaspora

AFAM 348.description: History of the environmental justice movement and the unequal distribution of environmental harms on low income, minority, and historically marginalized groups.
AFAM 348.subject: AFAM
AFAM 348.title: Environmental Racism and Justice

AFAM 350.description: Basic concepts, issues, and practices of antiracist education. Topics include individual and institutional racism, overt and covert racism, curriculum, textbooks, power relationships, teacher-student relationships, and privacy.
AFAM 350.subject: AFAM
AFAM 350.title: Antiracist Education

AFAM 353.description: Survey of theories of the impact of race, ethnicity, and racism on American politics, and analysis of major policies and racial group experience regarding American citizenship.
AFAM 353.subject: AFAM
AFAM 353.title: Introduction to U.S. Racial and Ethnic Politics

AFAM 355.description: Theoretical and empirical approaches related to race/ethnicity and the current state of race relations in America, with some attention to global issues.
AFAM 355.subject: AFAM
AFAM 355.title: Race and Ethnic Relations

AFAM 364.description: African-American politics from the colonial period to the present. Emphasis on voting rights and strategies to advance black representation.
AFAM 364.subject: AFAM
AFAM 364.title: African-American Politics

AFAM 378.description: An introduction to traditional and popular music styles from several cultures and regions in Africa as well as the African diaspora.
AFAM 378.subject: AFAM
AFAM 378.title: Music of the African World

AFAM 380.description: Roots of rap/hip hop music from African bardic tradition to African American vernacular traditions and development as a musical genre; rap’s musical and verbal traits and political ideologies; hip hop’s influence on mainstream American society and global youth.
AFAM 380.subject: AFAM
AFAM 380.title: Cultural History of Hip Hop Music

AFAM 382.description: A survey of the musical and artistic contributions of Black women from several musical traditions and eras, partially inspired by the visual album Lemonade released by Beyoncé Knowles Carter in 2016.
AFAM 382.subject: AFAM
AFAM 382.title: Lemonade and Beyond: Black Women's Agency and Community Building Through Musical Performance

AFAM 384.description: A study of fine art, craft, and material culture made by people of African descent in the United States from the 17th century to the present, accounting for African American artistic innovation and creativity as it has influenced art production globally.
AFAM 384.subject: AFAM
AFAM 384.title: African American Art

AFAM 386.description: An introduction to Black creative art making, community building, performance, and critique as a means of creating new visual cultures. Aims to critically examine race and representations through the mediums of visual art, dance and movement cannons, performance art, photography, architecture, and film.
AFAM 386.subject: AFAM
AFAM 386.title: Working Through a Visual Archive of Blackness: Performative Practices of Making and Presenting

AFAM 393.description: Draws on science fiction to understand the contemporary history of American racial and ethnic politics and to speculate about the significance of race in America’s political future.
AFAM 393.subject: AFAM
AFAM 393.title: Race and Science Fiction

AFAM 397.description: Reading and research on selected social and historical topics in African American studies. May be repeated as content varies by title.
AFAM 397.subject: AFAM
AFAM 397.title: Special Topics in African American Society and History

AFAM 398.description: Reading and research on selected arts and cultural topics in African-American studies. May be repeated as content varies by title.
AFAM 398.subject: AFAM
AFAM 398.title: Special Topics in African-American Arts and Cultures

AFAM 399.description: Contract approved by instructor, advisor, and department chair is required for undergraduate students.
AFAM 399.subject: AFAM
AFAM 399.title: Independent Study

AFAM 402.description: Survey of many of the major schools of historic and contemporary African American political thought.
AFAM 402.subject: AFAM
AFAM 402.title: African American Political Thought

AFAM 420.description: Interdisciplinary analysis of how the experiences of enslaved people are represented through fiction, autobiography, film, art, and new media.
AFAM 420.subject: AFAM
AFAM 420.title: Slavery, Literature Culture

AFAM 428A.description: Representative works of African-American writers to 1903.
AFAM 428A.subject: AFAM
AFAM 428A.title: African-American Literature I: to 1903

AFAM 428B.description: Representative works of African-American writers from 1903 to the present.
AFAM 428B.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ENGL 101, ENGL 102, and one course between ENGL 270 - ENGL 292.
AFAM 428B.subject: AFAM
AFAM 428B.title: African-American Literature II: 1903 – Present

AFAM 438D.description: Authors and literary forms representative of Africa.
AFAM 438D.subject: AFAM
AFAM 438D.title: African Literature

AFAM 438E.description: Authors and literary forms representative of the Caribbean.
AFAM 438E.subject: AFAM
AFAM 438E.title: Caribbean Literature

AFAM 442.description: Linguistic examination of the structure, history, and use of African-American English, as well as literary presentations, language attitudes, and issues relating to education and the acquisition of Standard English.
AFAM 442.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ENGL 101 and ENGL 102, and one course between ENGL 270-ENGL 292.
AFAM 442.subject: AFAM
AFAM 442.title: African-American English

AFAM 443.description: An examination of the political cracks, cultural changes, and liberation-focused collaborations between African Americans and Asian Americans in the contemporary period, including recent theoretical frameworks that bring Blackness and Asianness into view together in a post-Civil Rights era.
AFAM 443.subject: AFAM
AFAM 443.title: AfroAsian Connections in American Culture

AFAM 444.description: A survey of the social and political developments in the United States through the diverse experiences of African American women from slavery to the twenty-first century. Situates the heroism, activism, and feminism of African American women within a global context.
AFAM 444.subject: AFAM
AFAM 444.title: African American Women in History: Rebels, Radicals, Revolutionaries and Black Girl Magic

AFAM 463.description: This course critically examines the continuities and discontinuities between Jim Crow and our current historical and political moment.
AFAM 463.subject: AFAM
AFAM 463.title: Jim Crow: Histories Revivals

AFAM 476.description: Critical review of theories of community organizing, grassroots activism, and social movements, and examination of contemporary forms of black activism.
AFAM 476.subject: AFAM
AFAM 476.title: Black Activism

AFAM 486.description: African-American rhetoric as manifested in speeches, essays, and other rhetorical artifacts.
AFAM 486.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: WGST 111 or WGST 112 or ANTH 102.
AFAM 486.subject: AFAM
AFAM 486.title: African-American Rhetoric

AFAM 487.description: An examination of literature by and about black women, including fiction, poetry, drama, and autobiography. This study will focus on issues that emerge from the creative representations of black women and the intersections of race, gender, sexuality, and class that interrogate what is both particular and universal experiences.
AFAM 487.subject: AFAM
AFAM 487.title: Black Women Writers

AFAM 488.description: Analysis of the poetry, drama, art, music, and essays of the Black Arts Movement during the 1960s and 1970s, and their impact on American politics, history, and culture.
AFAM 488.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ENGL 101 and ENGL 102.
AFAM 488.subject: AFAM
AFAM 488.title: The Black Arts Movement

AFAM 503.description: An interdisciplinary examination of the historical and current functioning of the American criminal justice system and the ways that society has created and applied different practices and standards of justice with regard to marginalized populations.
AFAM 503.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in AFAM 201.
AFAM 503.subject: AFAM
AFAM 503.title: Miscarriages of Justice

AFAM 515.description: Representations of race and gender in comics with a special emphasis on the experiences of African Americans.
AFAM 515.subject: AFAM
AFAM 515.title: Race, Gender, and Graphic Novels

AFAM 517.description: Cultural representations, constructions, production, and consumption of African-American identity in the popular culture medium of feature films.
AFAM 517.subject: AFAM
AFAM 517.title: An Anthropological View of Blacks in Film

AFAM 565.description: The major movements, figures, plays, and critical strategies that have marked the development of African American theatre in the 19th, 20th, and 21st centuries.
AFAM 565.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ENGL 101, ENGL 102, and one course between ENGL 270 - ENGL 292.
AFAM 565.subject: AFAM
AFAM 565.title: African American Theatre

AFAM 580.description: Students will explore the African Diaspora as a social, cultural, and historical formation with Africa at its center, focusing on US, Latin American, and Caribbean African-descended communities.
AFAM 580.subject: AFAM
AFAM 580.title: Culture and Identity in the African Diaspora

AFAM 798.description: Reading and research on selected topics in African American Studies. May be repeated as content varies by title.
AFAM 798.subject: AFAM
AFAM 798.title: Advanced Topics in African American Studies
